run.question: List the top 5 largest Elasticsearch indices matching the pattern 'app-184-*' by document count. Show their names and doc counts.

report.summary: Of the 1,800 Elasticsearch indices matching the pattern 'app-184-*' (source otel-demo, target m0-otel-20260909), the largest document count is 500, and exactly five indices hold that count — so the top 5 is unambiguous, not a tie-break of many. The five are: app-184-security-auth-2024.01.05 (500 docs), app-184-platform-billing-2024.01.15 (500 docs), app-184-ml-worker-2024.01.25 (500 docs), app-184-engineering-api-2024.01.20 (500 docs) and app-184-data-analytics-2024.01.10 (500 docs). All five report health green and status open. Note that index listings carry no time range: these are the counts at query time (observed 2026-11-23T19:21:59Z / 19:22:01Z), and they cannot prove what the counts were during the historical window 2026-10-24T19:21:30Z–2026-11-23T19:21:30Z. No incident, alert or fault was under investigation here; this is a pure inventory count.

claims.text: The pattern 'app-184-*' matched 1,800 indices in the otel-demo Elasticsearch cluster (the jq 'length' over the returned list was 1800, and the over-limit result reported total_rows 1800).

Across those matched indices the maximum docs.count is 500, and exactly 5 indices have that count (max_docs 500, count_at_max 5), so the top 5 by document count is a unique set of five rather than an arbitrary slice of a larger tie.

Sorting the matched indices by docs.count descending yields, in order: app-184-security-auth-2024.01.05 (500), app-184-platform-billing-2024.01.15 (500), app-184-ml-worker-2024.01.25 (500), app-184-engineering-api-2024.01.20 (500), app-184-data-analytics-2024.01.10 (500).

The first rows of the docs.count-descending listing show all five top indices with health green, status open and store sizes between 30kb and 47.9kb: app-184-ml-worker-2024.01.25 47.8kb, app-184-data-analytics-2024.01.10 30kb, app-184-engineering-api-2024.01.20 47.9kb, app-184-security-auth-2024.01.05 46.9kb, app-184-platform-billing-2024.01.15 46.7kb.

All five top indices report health 'green' and status 'open'; the index listing shows no red/yellow health or closed index among the top 5, so this request is answered without any observed index-health anomaly.

gaps: The index listing has no time range: the doc counts are a point-in-time reading (observed 2026-11-23T19:21:59Z and 19:22:01Z) and do not show the counts during the incident window 2026-10-24T19:21:30Z to 2026-11-23T19:21:30Z.
Rows 5-1799 of the docs.count-descending listing were not read individually (the slice was truncated at 5 of 1800 rows), so the ranking below position 5 is unknown from this investigation.

Two jq attempts using the dotted path .docs.count returned null/errors because the field name contains a dot; the results above were produced with .["docs.count"], and no conclusion rests on the failed attempts.
next_steps: If a ranking beyond the top 5 is needed, read further slices of the stored listing (evidence_id 9809499f-2f99-48b8-ab98-627a147f1193-t0:5ec7158d-04f4-4e48-98fc-326d910f9500) with read_evidence at higher offsets, or re-query with jq sorting on .["docs.count"].

If historical doc counts are needed, query the indices with a time-scoped tool (for example elasticsearch_index_stats or elasticsearch_cat with index level) at the desired times rather than relying on this point-in-time listing.
